gloss: to excavate; to unearth; to discover

definitions.gloss: to excavate; to dig up; to unearth
definitions.explanation: To dig out something buried in the ground, especially archaeological remains, fossils, or resources.

definitions.gloss: to discover; to find (talent or potential)
definitions.explanation: To find and bring to light something previously unknown or unrecognized, especially hidden talent or ability.

examples.japanese: {古代|こだい}の{遺跡|いせき}を{発掘|はっくつ}する。
{工事中|こうじちゅう}に{土器|どき}が{発掘|はっくつ}された。
この{地域|ちいき}では{長年|ながねん}にわたって{発掘調査|はっくつちょうさ}が{行|おこな}われている。
examples.english: Excavation surveys have been conducted in this area for many years.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{才能|さいのう}を{発掘|はっくつ}する。
オーディションで{若|わか}い{歌手|かしゅ}を{発掘|はっくつ}した。
examples.english: A young singer was discovered at an audition.

examples.japanese: {地方|ちほう}の{小|ちい}さな{町|まち}から{世界的|せかいてき}なアーティストが{発掘|はっくつ}されることもある。
examples.english: Sometimes world-class artists are discovered from small rural towns.

notes:
The literal meaning of digging up (sense 1) extends naturally to the figurative meaning of discovering hidden talent (sense 2). Both senses are commonly used in news and everyday conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {発掘調査|はっくつちょうさ}: excavation survey; archaeological dig
- {発掘現場|はっくつげんば}: excavation site
- {人材|じんざい}を{発掘|はっくつ}する: to discover talented people
- {化石|かせき}を{発掘|はっくつ}する: to excavate fossils
- {才能|さいのう}の{発掘|はっくつ}: talent scouting; discovery of talent

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {掘|ほ}る: to dig — the basic verb for digging; physical action only
- {発見|はっけん}する: to discover — general discovery, not specifically digging up or finding talent
- {採掘|さいくつ}する: to mine; to extract — specifically for mining minerals and resources
